title: A Dragonfly Catches 95% of What It Hunts. A Lion Gets 25%

scenes.text: A dragonfly catches 95 percent of what it hunts. A lion gets 25.
Great white sharks miss about half their attacks. The dragonfly almost never misses.
It flies at 30 miles an hour and snatches prey straight out of the air.
Each eye has 30,000 lenses. In the lab, one ate 30 flies in a row and wanted more.
Its brain predicts where the prey will be and flies there. Like a guided missile.
The deadliest hunter on Earth is the size of your finger.

description:
Dragonflies catch their airborne prey more than 95 percent of the time, while African lions succeed on roughly 25 percent of hunts and great white sharks fail about half of theirs.
Flying at up to 30 miles an hour with 30,000-lens eyes, a dragonfly tracks a target and flies to where it will be, not where it is. In greenhouse trials some species caught 97 out of 100 fruit flies.
Which animal did you think was the best hunter before this?
first_comment: A circuit of just 16 neurons links the dragonfly's eyes to its wings to steer the interception. If you could borrow one animal's hunting skill, which would it be?
